description: Multi-category and flexible-range filtering on the movements list API
steps: Extend `GET /api/movements` so the category filter accepts more than one value: support `category_id` repeated (`?category_id=3&category_id=7`) and a comma-separated `category_id=3,7` form, parsing both into a deduplicated list of positive ints (silently dropping non-numeric/non-positive tokens); a single `category_id` keeps working exactly as today (the Dashboard recent-movements call and existing tests must stay green), and the resulting SQL uses `m.category_id = ANY($n)` when one or more ids are present

Add an `uncategorized` boolean query param: when `uncategorized=true` is sent alone, filter to `m.category_id IS NULL`; when sent alongside category ids, widen the predicate to `(m.category_id = ANY($n) OR m.category_id IS NULL)` so a user can review categorized + uncategorized rows together — keep the existing `from`/`to`/`store`/`search`/`payment_method_id`/`page`/`limit` params untouched and AND-combined with the category predicate

Add aggregate fields to the list response so the table header can show period totals without a second round-trip: alongside the existing `{ data, total, page, limit }`, return `totalAmount` (SUM of `amount` across the entire filtered set, not just the current page, as a number) — computed in the same `WHERE`-filtered query that already produces `total`

Raise the page-size ceiling for this list view: keep `limit` defaulting to 20 but allow up to 200 (was 100) so a month of movements fits in one or two pages; clamp out-of-range values as today and leave `page` semantics unchanged

API tests (Jest): repeated and comma-separated `category_id` both produce an IN/ANY filter; single `category_id` unchanged; `uncategorized=true` alone and combined with ids; `totalAmount` equals the full-set sum across multiple pages (independent of `limit`/`page`); category filter composes correctly with `from`/`to`; invalid category tokens are ignored rather than 400-ing

description: Filter-aware spend-over-time series endpoint for an arbitrary date range
steps: Add `GET /api/movements/series` returning a bucketed spend time series for an explicit `from`/`to` ISO-date range (both required; 400 with a clear message when missing, malformed, or `from > to`); it accepts the SAME filter params as the list endpoint — multi `category_id` (repeated + CSV), `uncategorized`, `store`, `search`, `payment_method_id` — and applies them identically so the chart always matches the table below it

Choose bucket granularity adaptively from the range span so the chart stays readable: span ≤ 1 day → hourly (`HH24:MI`), ≤ 92 days → daily (`YYYY-MM-DD`), ≤ ~730 days → weekly (ISO week, label `YYYY-MM-DD` of the week start), longer → monthly (`Mon YYYY`); return the chosen unit as `granularity` in the response so the client can format ticks

Fill empty buckets with zero via `generate_series` over the `[from, to]` bounds (reuse the existing dashboard pattern of LEFT JOIN-ing movements onto generated buckets with `DATE_TRUNC`), so a category with sporadic spend still renders a continuous trend line; each point is `{ label, total }` (total as a number) ordered chronologically

Include a previous-period comparison block computed over the equal-length window immediately preceding `[from, to]` with the same filters applied: `{ previousTotal, currentTotal, deltaPct }` (deltaPct null when previousTotal is 0) so the header can render a ▲/▼ trend telling the user whether the selected category's spend rose or fell versus the prior comparable window

Factor the label-format/granularity choice into a small shared helper (e.g. `api/src/helpers/timeSeries.ts`) used by this endpoint; keep the existing `/api/dashboard` series behavior byte-for-byte unchanged. API tests: granularity boundaries (1 day / 92 days / 730 days), zero-fill of gap buckets, category + payment-method filters reflected in totals, previous-period delta sign and null-on-zero, and 400s on bad/inverted ranges

description: Movements page with period and custom date-range selection
steps: Add a `/movements` route, a 'Movements' link in the persistent nav (between Dashboard and Import), and a client API wrapper `getMovementsSeries(params)` plus extend `GetMovementsParams`/`getMovements` to send `category_id` as a list and the `uncategorized` flag (axios `paramsSerializer` emitting repeated `category_id` params) and to read back the new `totalAmount`

Build the period control by reusing `PeriodSelector`'s exported helpers (`getPeriodLabel`, `navigatePeriod`, `isNextDisabled`): expose Day / Week / Month chips with ‹ › anchor navigation, and add a 'Custom range' mode that reveals two native date inputs (from / to). Selecting Day/Week/Month derives `from`/`to` from period+anchor (mirroring the dashboard's range math); Custom range sends the inputs directly. Validate `from ≤ to` inline. Do this without altering Dashboard's current `PeriodSelector` usage or its tests (additive props / a thin wrapper component — Year/All are out of scope for this page)

Persist the view in URL query params (`period`+`anchor`, or `from`+`to` for custom, plus category filter and page) via `useSearchParams` so the period, range, and filters survive reload and are shareable; default to the current month on first load

Render the full movements table fed by `GET /api/movements` for the resolved range: columns Date (+ time when present), Store / Description, Category badge (colored chip, em-dash when uncategorized), Payment method badge, and Amount (right-aligned, `$` formatted); a header row shows the period label, total movement count, and `totalAmount`; clicking a row opens the existing `MovementForm` for edit and a save refreshes the list; include loading skeletons, a 'No movements in this period' empty state, and pagination (page controls or a 'Load more' that appends) honoring the 200 max page size

Client tests (Vitest, mocked api module): Day/Week/Month chip + ‹ › navigation maps to the right `from`/`to`; Custom range inputs map to `from`/`to` with `from ≤ to` validation; URL params round-trip; table renders columns incl. uncategorized and time; header total/count reflect `totalAmount`/`total`; row click opens the edit form and save refetches; pagination appends; empty state

description: Category multi-select filter with a spend-over-time trend header
steps: Above the movements table, add a category filter control: a dropdown/popover listing every category (colored swatch + name, from `getCategories`) plus an 'Uncategorized' pseudo-option, each toggleable (multi-select); selected categories render as removable chips with an 'All categories' reset, and the selection drives both the list and the series queries (mapping to repeated `category_id` + the `uncategorized` flag) and is mirrored into the URL

Add a 'Spend over time' chart header above the table (recharts, matching the Dashboard's card styling) driven by `GET /api/movements/series` for the active range AND active category filter, so the curve reflects exactly the rows in the table; bars/area use the single category's color when exactly one category is selected and the primary color otherwise; tooltip shows the bucket label and `$`-formatted total; x-axis ticks formatted per the response `granularity`

In the chart header, show the period `currentTotal` and a trend pill from the series `deltaPct`: ▲ green when spend increased vs the previous comparable window, ▼ red when it decreased, with the percentage and a 'vs previous {period}' caption (hidden when `previousTotal` is 0 / delta null) — this is the core 'did spending for this category go up or down' signal called out in the ticket

Keep table, header total, and chart in sync on every change: switching period/range, navigating ‹ ›, or editing the category selection refetches both `/api/movements` and `/api/movements/series` with one shared params object; show a lightweight fetching state on the chart and table without flashing the whole page; render a friendly 'No spend to chart for this selection' state when the series is all zeros

Client tests: toggling categories updates repeated `category_id`/`uncategorized` in both list and series calls and the URL; chip removal and 'All categories' reset; single-category chart uses that category's color; trend pill direction/percentage from `deltaPct` (up, down, hidden on null); x-axis formatting follows `granularity`; chart + table refetch together when the period or filter changes
